memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light so that the lamps may be kept burning." - Exodus 27:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lamps in the Holy Place needed oil, and God tells the people where it comes from: they must bring it. Clear oil of pressed olives, the best quality, supplied by the community. The light did not maintain itself. Someone had to press the olives, and someone had to carry the oil.

Notice what pressing means. Olives do not give up their oil easily; they must be crushed. The very thing that produced light for God's dwelling came out of something being pressed. That is worth remembering when life presses hard on us. Paul spoke of being hard pressed on every side but not crushed, carrying around the death of Jesus so that His life might also be revealed (2 Cor 4:8-10). Pressure, in God's hands, is not wasted.

There is also a call to participation here. God could have provided oil miraculously; instead He asked His people to bring it. He invites us into the work rather than doing everything over our heads. The light in God's house depended on ordinary Israelites doing ordinary work faithfully. What has God asked you to bring so that His light keeps burning where you are?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What has God asked me to bring or do so that His light keeps burning?
Can I trust that God uses even the pressing seasons to produce something valuable?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You use even the pressing to produce light. Help me trust You in hard seasons, and show me what I should be bringing so that Your light keeps burning. Amen.
